# Kaval.AI

> An opinionated Python library for building production-grade agentic
> workflows, chatbots and tools. A workflow is a typed graph — written as YAML
> or built in Python — executed by an engine that validates every boundary with
> Pydantic and records every session, run, node and model call in a database
> the operator owns. The same engine runs on a server, in a test suite and in a
> browser tab through Pyodide and WebLLM.

Install with `pip install "kavalai[common]"`. Provider clients are selected by
a `provider/model` string (`openai/…`, `gemini/…`, `anthropic/…`, `ollama/…`).
Source: https://github.com/Kaval-AI/kaval.ai — Apache-2.0.

## Start here

- [Architecture](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/architecture.html): the design, its commitments, the component diagram and the invariants a change must respect. Read this before proposing a structural change.
- [Installation](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/installation.html): packages, extras and provider configuration.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/quickstart.html): a working chatbot workflow, in Python and in YAML.
- [Concepts](https://docs.kaval.ai/guides/concepts.html): the vocabulary of language-model applications.

## Tutorials

- [LLM clients](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/llm_clients.html): one interface over four providers; structured output, streaming, retries, usage statistics.
- [Agents and tools](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/agents.html): the tool-using agent loop, typed inputs and outputs, restricting tools per node.
- [Workflows](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/workflow.html): the graph, branching, agent nodes, parallel fan-out, rendered diagrams, testing without a model.
- [RAG](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/rag.html): indexing and retrieval over pgvector or a portable SQLite file.
- [Streaming](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/streamer.html): model tokens, per-node run events and Server-Sent Events.
- [Observability and storage](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/observability_storage.html): sessions, runs, chat history and swapping the backend.
- [Serving over HTTP](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/serving.html): any workflow behind a typed FastAPI endpoint.
- [Running in the browser](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/run_in_browser.html): Pyodide and WebLLM, with no server and no API key.

## Guides

- [Workflows](https://docs.kaval.ai/guides/workflows.html): the workflow model in depth.
- [Tools](https://docs.kaval.ai/guides/tools.html): Python functions, REST endpoints and MCP servers through one kernel.
- [Agents](https://docs.kaval.ai/guides/agents.html): how the agent loop plans, acts and observes.
- [Observability](https://docs.kaval.ai/guides/observability.html): what a run records, and why there is no cost column.
- [Evaluation and acceptance testing](https://docs.kaval.ai/guides/evaluation.html): grading a running agent with literal matchers or a judging model, and why the case file never names the server.
- [The database and data model](https://docs.kaval.ai/guides/data_model.html): every runtime table, what it holds and how the schema is created.
- [Safety and determinism](https://docs.kaval.ai/guides/safety.html): running a graph with no network and no API key.

## Reference

- [Workflow YAML reference](https://docs.kaval.ai/reference/yaml.html): every key of the workflow document.
- [Evaluation YAML and CLI](https://docs.kaval.ai/reference/eval_yaml.html): every key of a case file, every matcher, and the `kavalai-eval` flags and exit codes.
- [Bundled tools](https://docs.kaval.ai/reference/tools.html): the tools shipped with the library.
- [Model providers](https://docs.kaval.ai/reference/providers.html): the LLM, embedding and RAG providers that ship with the library, where each one publishes its model names, and how to list them from the SDK.
- [Configuration](https://docs.kaval.ai/reference/config.html): every environment variable the entry points read.
- [Agent skills](https://docs.kaval.ai/reference/skills.html): the briefings shipped for coding agents, and `kavalai-skills install`.
- [Python API](https://docs.kaval.ai/api/index.html): generated API documentation.
- [Cookbook](https://docs.kaval.ai/cookbook/index.html): worked recipes, from retrieval to self-correcting loops, plus two worked evaluations — a RAG chatbot and a workflow with side effects.

## Optional

- [How Kaval.AI compares](https://docs.kaval.ai/tutorials/comparison.html): an assessment against LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI, n8n and Dify, including where Kaval.AI is behind.
- [Backoffice UI](https://docs.kaval.ai/ui/index.html): the interface that browses recorded runs.
- [Deployment](https://docs.kaval.ai/deploy/index.html): containers, migrations and configuration.
